transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Lee. It's really nice to meet you, and thank you so much for fitting me in. 

Um... well, I hope I'm explaining this right, but I guess I'm here because things got a little out of hand at work? I mean, usually working hard is a good thing, right? But I went from just being a normal crew guy doing landscaping to suddenly trying to run, like, three different bids at once. I was calling city people, lining up all these plant suppliers, and just messaging everybody I knew about this big park idea I had. 

I just... I couldn't really shut it off. I guess I took it a little too far and worried some people. Does that make sense as a reason to be here? I really don't want to waste your time.
Have you been using any drugs or substances recently, like cocaine, amphetamines, or other stimulants?

Oh! No, no, definitely not. I promise I haven't been doing anything like that. No drugs, no cocaine or... or any of those stimulants. 

I mean, I know it probably sounds like I was on something, right? With how crazy I was acting at work and all the energy I had. But I swear, I don't touch any of that stuff. Just, you know, regular coffee before my shift, but that's it. I hope you believe me... I really try to be a responsible guy and stay out of trouble. Is... is that what you needed to know?

During this time when you were full of energy and plans, did you ever notice anything unusual—like hearing voices, seeing things others didn't, or having beliefs that others thought were false or paranoid?

Oh, no. No, definitely not. Um... I know I was acting pretty intense, but I wasn't... I wasn't hearing voices or seeing things that weren't there. I promise. 

And my ideas for the park, they were just, you know, regular landscaping things. Actual trees and benches, not anything weird or... or paranoid. My boss and the guys just thought it was way too much all at once, which, you know, they were right about. But I wasn't making things up in my head or anything like that. 

I hope you don't think I'm, like, completely losing my mind? I just got really, really wrapped up in the work and wanted to do a good job. Is... is it a good sign that I wasn't seeing things? I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers so you can help me.

How many days in a row has this high-energy, non-stop period lasted, and has it caused serious problems—like missing work, financial risk, or needing others to step in—rather than just being unusually productive?

Um... well, it lasted about two weeks, I think? Yeah, around two weeks of just being super fired-up and feeling like I could take on the world. It started when I decided I needed to totally remake myself to pitch this park idea. I was just... I was so excited, you know? 

But as for serious problems... I mean, I really don't want to make it sound worse than it was. I didn't get fired or anything! My boss just had to sit me down and tell me to back off because I was overwhelming the clients and the suppliers. I guess I was being a bit much, and they had to kind of step in and smooth things over with the city people. 

I didn't mean to cause any trouble, I swear. I just wanted to do a really good job. But then after those two weeks, I just... I completely crashed. Like, couldn't get out of bed crashed. 

Does that... does that answer your question okay? I hope it doesn't make me sound like a bad employee. I really do try to be reliable.
Before these past two weeks, have you ever had another period—lasting days or weeks—where you felt unusually high-energy and elated, or on the flip side, deeply depressed, low, or unable to function?

Um... well, before these last couple of weeks where I had all that energy... I haven't really had another time where I felt that high, no. This was the first time I felt that... that fired up.

But, um... as for feeling low... yeah. I, uh... I don't like to complain, you know? I really try to just push through and be a hard worker. But... honestly, I've been feeling pretty down for... gosh, maybe about a year now? It's just been this sort of heavy feeling hanging over me. I still went to work and did my best, I promise! I didn't let it ruin my job or anything. 

But this crash after the two weeks of energy... this is definitely the worst the depression has gotten. I just... I couldn't even move. I feel terrible about it, like I should just be stronger, you know? I hope you don't think I'm just being lazy. It's just really hard sometimes. Does... does that make sense? I'm trying to give you the whole picture so you can figure out what's wrong with me.

{"intent": "Determine whether the patient is currently in an active depressive episode (to assess current mood state and any mixed features) versus the depression having resolved after the high-energy period.", "question": "Right now, today, are you still feeling that deep, low, unable-to-move kind of depression you described after your energetic period, or has that lif

Um... right now, today? Well... I'm doing okay, I think. I mean, I made it here to see you, right? So that's good. 

I'm definitely not stuck in bed like I was right after that really intense couple of weeks. That was... that was pretty bad. But today, I wouldn't say I'm completely unable to move or anything like that. I'm trying really hard to get back to normal and be productive again. 

I still feel a little... heavy, maybe? Like things are just a bit harder than they should be. But I don't want to make a big deal out of it if it's just regular tiredness. I'm really trying to keep a good attitude about it. Do you think it's normal to still feel a little sluggish after all that? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right things to get better.

During that crash when you couldn't get out of bed, did you also notice things like your thoughts still racing, feeling restless or agitated, or not needing much sleep, all happening at the same time as the low mood?

Um... no, no, I don't think so. When I crashed, I really just... crashed. 

I wasn't restless or agitated or anything like that. I didn't have racing thoughts either. My mind was actually pretty... blank, I guess? I just felt really heavy and tired, and I was sleeping a lot. Like, way more than usual. I definitely wasn't having trouble sleeping or feeling like I didn't need it. 

I just kind of shut down completely. I hope that's... I mean, is that the right way to respond to that kind of thing? I wasn't trying to be difficult or cause problems by sleeping so much, my body just felt like it gave out. I really hope I'm not making things sound too confusing for you.
During that time when you couldn't get out of bed, did you have any thoughts of wanting to hurt yourself or wishing you weren't alive?

Um... gosh. I... I really hate to admit this, honestly. I don't want you to think I'm crazy or, you know, ungrateful for my life or anything. I really try to be a positive guy. 

But... yeah. It got pretty dark. Usually, if I've been feeling down in the past, I might just wish I could disappear for a while. Just go to sleep and not have to deal with the heavy feeling, you know? But during that really bad crash... I actually got really scared of myself. 

I was sitting out in my work truck after my shift, and... well, I realized I wasn't just wishing I could disappear anymore. I was sitting there looking around, thinking about exactly how I could end it with the gear and stuff I had right there in the truck with me. 

I didn't do anything, obviously! I swear I wouldn't actually do that. I know better. It just... my brain just went there, and it terrified me. I'm so sorry, I know that’s probably really alarming to hear, and I feel ashamed even saying it out loud. I just want to make sure I’m giving you the whole truth so you know what's going on. You don't think I'm a lost cause for thinking like that, do you?
Right now, today, are you having any thoughts of wanting to hurt yourself or end your life?

Oh, no, no. Definitely not today. I promise. 

Like I said, I'm doing a lot better right now. I'm trying really hard to stay positive and keep moving forward. It was really just... just that one time in the truck when things got so bad that I was actually looking at my gear and figuring out how to do it. That was the only time it went from just wishing I could sleep forever to actually... planning something out. 

But right now? Today? No, I'm not having any thoughts like that at all. I want to be here, and I want to get better. I hope you believe me. I really don't want you to worry about me doing something drastic today. I'm safe, I promise. Is it okay that I'm just focusing on the positive right now?
